div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY LOCAL-FIRST?
Problem: coding depends on the exact checkout, uncommitted files, toolchain, credentials, processes, and OS behavior.
Chosen: keep control, execution, history, checkpoints, and UI on the developer machine; only configured LLM/MCP calls leave it.
Why not hosted-first: repo mirroring creates state drift, privacy exposure, latency, tenancy infrastructure, and a second environment that may not reproduce the bug.
Consequence: high fidelity and user-owned evidence; execution shares the user trust domain, so policy, confirmation, rollback, and honest sandbox labeling are mandatory.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY PYTHON WITH NATIVE-BACKED HOT PATHS?
Problem: model SDKs and AI integrations evolve faster than the product can afford binding lag.
Chosen: Python for orchestration and contributor velocity; C/Rust-backed parsing, tokenization, serialization, Git, and package resolution where throughput matters.
Why not a Rust rewrite: stronger static guarantees are attractive, but provider lag, FFI work, and contributor cost dominate now.
Consequence: fast adaptation in exchange for disciplined boundaries, profiling, and explicit concurrency control.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY TEXTUAL/RICH AS THE PRESENTATION STACK?
Problem: long agent runs need incremental components, keyboard control, live metrics, diffs, and confirmations without leaving the terminal.
Chosen: Textual supplies a stateful async widget/application model; Rich supplies mature terminal rendering primitives.
Why not hand-written ANSI: focus, resize, layout, and platform behavior become product code. Why not a browser frontend: Node/server/IPC packaging exceeds the local workflow need.
Consequence: a real operational UI from Python; terminal capability variance and Textual-specific lifecycle complexity remain.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY JSON SETTINGS, UV ENVIRONMENTS, AND HATCHLING BUILDS?
JSON: strict ubiquitous interchange for CLI, schemas, automation, and model-readable configuration. uv: fast reproducible bootstrap/resolution without making its environment wrapper the product runtime. Hatchling: small standards-based wheel/sdist backend.
Why not one all-owning packaging framework or custom config DSL: environment management, build publication, and user configuration have different responsibilities.
Consequence: replaceable boring layers and fast onboarding; JSON sacrifices comments and uv remains an external developer tool.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY LOCAL EVENT-DERIVED OBSERVABILITY?
Problem: agent failures are often contextual—wrong file, lost goal, repeated tool loop—not ordinary exceptions. The operator needs to reconstruct what the model saw and what the machine did.
Chosen: metrics, cards, audit, and logs are projections of the same local event/evidence plane; prompt compaction never deletes the operator trace.
Why not cloud-only telemetry: source, commands, paths, and outputs may be private; network availability should not determine debuggability. Why not raw logs only: humans need semantic grouping and live progress.
Consequence: privacy-aligned postmortems and trust; local retention, redaction, and disk usage remain product responsibilities.

div.style: color: rgb(30, 41, 59) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Reviewable completion evidence
task contract/status · test observations · diffs
files/checkpoints · full causal ledger

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY IS THE FINAL MODEL MESSAGE THE LIFECYCLE BOUNDARY?
Problem: the user needs one observable event that means the agent has stopped acting. A hidden validator veto previously risked leaving the controller RUNNING with no next action.
Chosen: explicit final prose is persisted, then FINISHED is published immediately.
Why not infer completion from silence or an empty tool queue: both can occur during failure or waiting. Why not a separate mandatory finish tool: plain response semantics already exist in chat/plan and providers; another tool creates a failure mode after work is done.
Consequence: clear liveness and UI behavior; the model may still finish prematurely.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY IS COMPLETION VALIDATION ADVISORY TODAY?
Problem: tests/diffs/task evidence are valuable, but no single validator reliably knows user intent, environment constraints, or whether a warning deserves another autonomous mutation.
Chosen: validators collect an independent quality signal after the final boundary and emit a durable warning.
Why not a hard veto without a recovery transition: it creates a non-terminal state with no actor responsible for the next step. A future hard gate would need an explicit reopen/replan protocol and bounded authority.
Consequence: liveness and evidence are separated; correctness is reviewable, not guaranteed by the state enum.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY SEPARATE EVIDENCE COLLECTION, QUALITY SIGNALING, AND LIFECYCLE AUTHORITY?
Evidence records what happened. Validation interprets whether evidence looks sufficient. Lifecycle decides whether more actions may occur.
Why not collapse them: a missing test result should not silently erase history, and a warning should not mutate the workspace without an accountable control transition.
Consequence: interview-defensible boundaries and safer future evolution; users must understand that FINISHED means execution ended, not mathematical proof of correctness.

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY ARE OBSERVATIONS FIRST-CLASS EVENTS?
Problem: an Action is only an intention; exit code, changed files, diagnostics, user denial, timeout, and external results determine reality.
Chosen: tools return typed, cause-linked Observations that are persisted and projected like Actions.
Why not return raw values directly to the caller: UI, retry, audit, context, and recovery would see different or incomplete outcomes.
Consequence: one evidence contract and exact latency/result attribution; observation schemas must represent partial and failed reality honestly.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY WAIT FOR THE WHOLE SCHEDULED BATCH?
Problem: prompting after the first of several parallel results makes the model reason from an intermediate world and potentially mutate a resource whose sibling action is still running.
Chosen: the next inference begins only after every cause-keyed pending action in the batch resolves or is classified.
Why not stream each result into a new model turn: more calls, nondeterministic context order, and race-amplified decisions.
Consequence: coherent batch snapshots and reproducible prompts; the slowest action sets batch latency.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY CLASSIFIED BOUNDED RETRY INSTEAD OF CATCH-ALL RETRY?
Problem: transient transport/storage/tool failures may recover, but deterministic syntax, permission, and logic failures repeat cost and side effects.
Chosen: retry only known recoverable categories, with attempt limits/backoff; circuit and recovery services own escalation.
Why not infinite self-healing: liveness becomes an expensive loop. Why not fail immediately: temporary faults would waste long session state.
Consequence: resilience with an explicit exhaustion boundary; taxonomy quality determines false retry/false failure rates.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY DO ONLY HARD STUCK SIGNALS CONTROL THE LOOP?
Problem: legitimate TDD, exploration, and refactoring often look repetitive semantically; heuristic interruption can stop the agent exactly when iteration is useful.
Chosen: exact repeated action/observation/error sequences and monologue/null-action limits may stop or redirect; semantic similarity and cost-growth guesses remain telemetry.
Why not an LLM judge every step: added cost and another probabilistic veto over liveness.
Consequence: fewer false-positive stops; subtle waste may be detected later.

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Policy is not isolation.
Interactive PTYs remain host processes; OS subprocess isolation is not a VM/container or complete host boundary.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A PRIVATE CONTENT-ADDRESSED GIT STORE FOR WORKSPACE CHECKPOINTS?
Problem: checkpoints must handle modified/untracked/binary files, work without a clean user repo, deduplicate unchanged content, and restore any prior tree.
Chosen: pygit2 writes commits to a separate bare object store; a stat cache avoids rereading unchanged files; no subprocess or user branch is touched.
Why not full directory copies: O(repo size) data per checkpoint. Why not user Git commits/stash: pollutes history, depends on repository state, and misses non-repo workspaces. Why not inverse patches: fragile for deletes, binaries, renames, and command side effects.
Consequence: incremental cross-platform snapshots and branch independence; libgit2 storage/GC and whole-tree enumeration still cost resources.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY QUARANTINE EXTRA FILES DURING RESTORE?
Problem: restoring an exact snapshot normally deletes files created later, but those files may contain valuable user work or crash evidence.
Chosen: move extras into a timestamped checkpoint-local quarantine, then atomically replace snapshot files.
Why not delete for perfect rollback: rollback should reduce harm, not introduce irreversible loss. Why not leave extras in place: the restored workspace would not match the checkpoint and tests could see mixed states.
Consequence: recoverable exactness; rollback consumes additional disk until quarantine is reviewed.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY AN IN-PROCESS LOCAL RUNTIME INSTEAD OF MANDATORY DOCKER/RPC?
Problem: the default single-user agent needs low-latency access to the actual shell, editors, language servers, credentials, and OS paths.
Chosen: RuntimeExecutor lives in the process but communicates through typed Action/Observation events as if it were a boundary.
Why not mandatory containers: startup, mounts, path translation, daemon availability, nested virtualization, and environment mismatch harm local fidelity. Why retain typed boundaries: a future isolated driver remains possible and faults are attributable.
Consequence: native performance and easy debugging; runtime faults share the host process and policy cannot be advertised as isolation.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A SMALL NATIVE FILE API WITH EXACT REPLACEMENT?
Problem: free-form patch/XML/JSON edits are easy for a model to almost format correctly and hard to make atomic across files.
Chosen: explicit paths; exact old→new anchors; create/replace/multiedit transactions implemented in code; reads/discovery remain separate.
Why not shell redirection or a universal editor DSL: escaping, encoding, partial writes, and ambiguous match behavior leak into model reasoning.
Consequence: deterministic failures and safer refactors; the model may need an extra read to obtain an exact anchor.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY TREE-SITTER PLUS LSP?
Tree-sitter gives fast, local, cross-language structure for indexing even when a project cannot build. LSP gives compiler-aware definitions, references, diagnostics, and types when a language server is available.
Why not LSP only: server startup/configuration can fail and broad indexing would be expensive. Why not parsing only: syntax cannot resolve dynamic/project-specific semantics.
Consequence: graceful structural baseline with optional semantic precision; two caches/invalidation paths must remain coherent.

div.style: color: rgb(30, 41, 59) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before non-trivial FileEdit/CmdRun or HIGH risk
tier-1 private shadow checkpoint

div.style: color: rgb(124, 45, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Dispatch approved Action to local RuntimeExecutor

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY DETERMINISTIC MIDDLEWARE AROUND A PROBABILISTIC MODEL?
Problem: prompting improves action selection but cannot guarantee cost, permission, safety, rollback, logging, or postcondition behavior.
Chosen: every tool proposal crosses an ordered execute/observe contract that can block before effects and reconcile after reality is known.
Why not embed all policy in each tool: rules drift and new tools bypass them. Why not prompt-only safety: a stochastic component cannot be the final authority over its own side effects.
Consequence: bounded blast radius and composable governance; middleware order is a compatibility contract and adds per-call overhead.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY DOES MIDDLEWARE ORDER MATTER?
Safety/progress/cost/context first reject actions that should never proceed. Rollback before destructive execution ensures recovery exists before mutation. Pre-diff/autocheck/diagnostics establish and verify edit consequences. Index/file state reconcile derived repository views. Logging/telemetry/validation record and judge the resulting observation.
Alternative rejected: unordered plugin hooks where a safety check can run after execution or a checkpoint after mutation.
Consequence: adding or moving middleware requires reasoning about temporal preconditions, not only feature ownership.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY RESOURCE-AWARE BOUNDED PARALLELISM?
Problem: independent reads and distinct-file edits can reduce latency, but concurrent conflicting mutations destroy deterministic state and observation order.
Chosen: classify actions; allow safe read mixes and same-category distinct resource keys; serialize opaque MCP, conflicts, and mixed side-effect categories; cap each batch and wait for all cause IDs.
Why not read-only parallelism only: leaves safe distinct-resource throughput unused. Why not parallelize everything: rollback, confirmation, prompts, and tests would observe races.
Consequence: speed where independence is provable; conservative serialization when identity or effects are opaque.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY CHECKPOINT BEFORE RISKY ACTIONS, NOT AFTER EVERY EVENT?
Problem: rollback must capture the last known-good workspace before mutation; read-only commands add no recovery value and would flood retention.
Chosen: middleware snapshots non-trivial file edits, commands, and HIGH-risk future action types; trivial read-only commands are recognized and skipped.
Why not after execution: too late. Why not every step: storage/time cost and a noisy checkpoint list. Why not only manual checkpoints: humans cannot predict every bad autonomous action.
Consequence: transaction-like safety around effects; classification errors can over-snapshot or leave a gap, so HIGH-risk metadata provides a generic fallback.

div.style: color: rgb(49, 46, 129) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

Strict ProviderResolver

div.style: color: rgb(30, 41, 59) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

Commit/remove streaming WAL only after
a complete response was decoded

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Restart with recent uncommitted streaming WAL:
block automatic retry as ambiguous
stale/corrupt policy may discard while preserving crash evidence

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY OWN A PROVIDER-NORMALIZATION BOUNDARY?
Problem: providers differ in streaming chunks, tool-call IDs, stop reasons, errors, parameters, caching, and endpoint conventions.
Chosen: native client families translate at one boundary into Grinta messages, usage, tool calls, and exceptions.
Why not scatter if-provider branches through the agent: orchestration behavior would change with transport details and every new model would touch core logic. Why not trust one universal wrapper blindly: lowest-common-denominator abstractions often hide meaningful semantics.
Consequence: portable engine and explicit compatibility; the adapter/catalog surface requires continuous maintenance.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY STRICT PROVIDER RESOLUTION?
Problem: model names are not globally unique and compatible gateways may expose arbitrary IDs. Guessing from substrings can send credentials or unsupported parameters to the wrong endpoint.
Chosen: explicit provider prefix/config, otherwise exact catalog lookup; ambiguity fails visibly.
Why not fuzzy convenience: a friendly misroute is more dangerous than a clear configuration error.
Consequence: deterministic security and support behavior; onboarding may require one explicit setting.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY DATA-DRIVEN CAPABILITIES INSTEAD OF MODEL-NAME CONDITIONS?
Problem: context size, parallel calls, parameter support, and pricing are properties that change independently of provider brand.
Chosen: catalog facts drive budgets and request shaping; provider-family code handles protocol semantics.
Why not checks like name contains claude: aliases, versions, and compatible hosts make folklore brittle.
Consequence: most compatibility updates become auditable data changes; stale catalogs remain an operational risk and conservative fallbacks are required.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A SECOND WRITE-AHEAD CHECKPOINT FOR LLM STREAMING?
Problem: after a crash mid-stream, the remote provider may have consumed the request and emitted partial content, but the local engine cannot know whether repeating it will duplicate cost or actions.
Chosen: write a small intent marker before the call and delete only after complete decode; recent uncommitted markers block guessing.
Why not persist the full prompt: secrets, size, and duplication of the event ledger. Why not retry automatically: the outcome is ambiguous, not proven failed.
Consequence: honest recovery and crash evidence; some sessions require explicit operator resolution.

div.style: color: rgb(88, 28, 135) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

Dynamic system messages placed before last user turn

user/assistant/tool roles normalized per provider

div.style: color: rgb(88, 28, 135) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mode/capability-filtered tool schemas
native core + optional LSP/web/docs/debug/MCP/checkpoint

div.style: color: rgb(49, 46, 129) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Final streaming request
stable prefix + dynamic state + current user turn
tools + output reservation + cache fingerprint

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
MCP catalog is a separate per-turn system message,
not part of the stable primary system prompt

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY TREAT PROMPTS AS PROGRAMS?
Problem: the prompt branches on OS, mode, capabilities, security, and configured tools. Hiding that logic in a template DSL makes control flow hard to test and review.
Chosen: Markdown owns static prose; Python owns conditions, ordering, validation, metrics, and composition.
Why not Jinja variants or one giant string: template branches create a second programming language; giant strings make section-level testing and budgeting opaque.
Consequence: ordinary debugging and unit tests; prompt changes remain production code and require regression discipline.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY THIS SYSTEM-PROMPT ORDER?
Identity/precedence first establishes authority. Mode defines the social contract before affordances. Shell prevents platform-invalid actions. Security before routing/tools frames capability with constraints. Routing before reference teaches choice, not merely availability. Autonomy governs multi-step persistence. Interaction defines legitimate pause. Critical rules last exploit recency for high-cost failure modes.
Consequence: the prompt is an ordered policy stack, not a bag of instructions; reordering can change behavior even with identical text.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY INCLUDE BOTH TOOL SCHEMAS AND TOOL GUIDANCE?
Schema says what arguments are syntactically legal. Routing/reference policy says when a tool is appropriate, which safer abstraction precedes shell, and what evidence to gather next.
Why not schemas alone: the model may choose a legal but unsafe/inefficient route. Why not prose-only pseudo-tools: provider-native validation and structured decoding are lost.
Consequence: machine-checkable calls plus human-readable decision policy; duplicated descriptions consume tokens and must stay aligned.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY CAPABILITY-GATED WORKED EXAMPLES?
Problem: examples teach multi-tool choreography more effectively than abstract rules, but they are expensive and can make chat/plan modes imitate edits they cannot perform.
Chosen: include edit-heavy examples only for agent mode, enabled editor, and models not classified small.
Why not always include them: small contexts lose useful history; restricted modes receive contradictory demonstrations.
Consequence: examples are treated as an optimization with a budget, not sacred prompt content.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY STABLE POLICY FIRST AND DYNAMIC DATA NEAR THE USER TURN?
Problem: repo state, MCP availability, status, and context packet change frequently. Putting them inside the primary system string invalidates provider prefix caches and makes historical dynamic snapshots look like permanent policy.
Chosen: fingerprint the stable leading system prefix + tool schemas; rebuild volatile application-owned messages once per request beside the latest user turn.
Why not append dynamic state forever: stale maps/status accumulate and compete with current truth.
Consequence: cache reuse and clearer authority; message ordering must be normalized for provider compatibility.

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Reduce events into deterministic CanonicalTaskState
load revisioned TaskState + pre-compaction snapshot

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 Recent user request context

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
7 Latest narrative summary
excluded if it is itself a packet/working-set marker

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
8 Recent causal tail
up to 10 non-message event details
section limit max(1,200 chars, 14%)

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
<CONTEXT_PACKET>
ordered sections under character budget
cached by events/state/snapshot fingerprint

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;
color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A CONTEXT PACKET IN ADDITION TO HISTORY?
Problem: chronological history answers what happened; the next model turn needs an explicit answer to what is true now and what should happen next. Recovering state by rereading every event consumes attention and encourages stale facts.
Chosen: a bounded, deterministic current-state packet beside the causal tail.
Why not replace history entirely: state without evidence hides how conclusions were reached and removes local tool-call detail.
Consequence: state + trajectory are complementary inputs; duplicated facts must be actively suppressed.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY EXACTLY THESE SECTIONS, IN THIS ORDER?
User request repairs intent lost by windowing. Execution contract defines completion truth. Compact snapshot restores the boundary immediately after loss. Operational checkpoint prevents restart hesitation. Canonical detail preserves blockers, decisions, failures, VCS, and tests. Active status prevents duplicate background commands. Narrative summary carries architectural arc. Recent tail provides local cause/effect.
Ordering principle: intent and obligation outrank narrative and recency when the packet cannot fit.
Consequence: the packet degrades toward task correctness rather than conversational completeness.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A SMALL CHARACTER-BUDGETED PACKET WITH PERCENTAGE CAPS?
Problem: authoritative state can itself grow until it crowds out code, history, and tool schemas.
Chosen: 6k baseline with cautious scaling for very large contexts; each category has a cap and assembly stops low-priority expansion.
Why characters here, tokens elsewhere: sections are mostly bounded prose/state and character slicing allows structural safe-cut logic; the outer prompt still receives tokenizer-aware accounting.
Why not equal shares: categories have unequal failure cost—losing the objective is worse than losing old narrative detail.
Consequence: predictable control-plane overhead; a very complex task may require the external task store or targeted recall rather than a larger packet.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY XML-LIKE MARKERS AND SAFE CLOSING TAGS?
Problem: dynamic data, old tool output, and user text can resemble instructions. Unclosed or silently clipped sections blur authority boundaries.
Chosen: typed markers such as CONTEXT_PACKET and EXECUTION_CONTRACT; truncation preserves both opening and closing tags and emits an explicit marker.
Why not free-form concatenation: models cannot reliably distinguish policy, state, evidence, and quoted source material.
Consequence: clearer prompt roles and easier inspection; tags are conventions, not a security sandbox, so runtime policy still enforces effects.

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Boundary tokens ≥ effective window
− reserved summary − fixed prompt reserve
or explicit /compact?

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Skip compaction
also suppress same-turn double compact and
recompact below last post-boundary size

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Active StructuredSummaryCompactor
max_size 102; target roughly half-size history
fold prior summary + older pruned events

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Reduce source material before summarization
group files · commands · errors · navigation
plus last 5 non-user raw events

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Compaction prompt
durable task state is read-only authority
goal context · latest verification · prior summary
event digest · recent raw detail

div.style: color: rgb(49, 46, 129) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Same active LLM, plain prose completion
budget min(5% context, 12k tokens)
retry short/empty output up to configured repair attempts

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Required priority
unresolved/blocking → next steps → failed approaches
→ accomplished/architecture → decisions/rationale
USER GOAL fallback only if durable task state absent

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CondensationAction establishes a new boundary
old raw events remain in ledger
prompt projection becomes summary + recent tail

div.style: color: rgb(136, 19, 55) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Canonical/fuzzy continuity comparison
telemetry warning today; non-empty summary is accepted

div.style: color: rgb(71, 85, 105) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Present in repository but not selected by current ContextPipeline:
observation masking · recent-events · smart importance
microcompact · composition pipeline

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A SUMMARY BOUNDARY INSTEAD OF DELETING EVENTS?
Problem: repeated windowing eventually hides too much of the operational arc for a fresh reasoning turn to understand how the present state emerged.
Chosen: synthesize older evidence into a bounded narrative checkpoint, then retain a raw recent tail; the immutable ledger still holds originals.
Why not permanently rewrite history: audit and postmortem truth would inherit summary errors. Why not keep unlimited raw context: cost, latency, attention dilution, and provider limits rise even with large windows.
Consequence: long-run continuity at bounded prompt cost; semantic loss is unavoidable and must be counterbalanced by deterministic state.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY THE CURRENT SINGLE PROSE COMPACTOR, NOT THE LEGACY AUTO-SELECTOR?
Chosen now: one active mechanism with one trigger and one boundary contract; free prose lets the model allocate space to the actual session shape, while a strict section priority preserves resumability.
Why not keep switching among masking, recency, semantic importance, and multi-layer pipelines: policy became difficult to predict, test, and explain; a wrong strategy firing is itself context risk.
Why not rigid schema output: field compliance can consume attention and omit cross-cutting narrative. Deterministic task/canonical state already owns structured truth.
Consequence: simpler operations and richer narrative; prose is less machine-verifiable and the current continuity gate warns rather than vetoes.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY GROUPED DIGEST + FIVE RAW EVENTS?
Grouped digest: changes the evidence shape from thousands of repetitive lines into counts and unique files/commands/errors, reducing recency bias and prompt size 5–10× in intended workloads. Five raw events: retain exact local detail near the boundary where the next action depends on it.
Why not send all pruned events to the summary model: the summarizer can overflow or focus on late verbosity. Why not digest only: exact error/path detail disappears.
Consequence: macro arc plus a narrow microscope; details outside both survive only in the ledger/canonical reducers.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY KEEP DURABLE TASK STATE OUT OF THE SUMMARY OUTPUT?
Problem: repeatedly copying objective, requirements, plan, and statuses into prose creates stale competing versions and goal drift.
Chosen: give durable task state to the compactor as read-only interpretation context, but re-inject the authoritative aggregate separately after compaction.
Why not let the summary own task truth: prose is lossy, model-generated, and replaced at every boundary.
Consequence: narrative memory can evolve while the task contract remains revisioned and inspectable.

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Resolve model capacity
usable input = context window − output reservation
subtract static prompt + tool schemas + context packet

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Project full durable history
filter non-model events
budget oversized tool results

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Tokenizer-aware event estimates
model correction factor
LRU cache by event fingerprint + rendering

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Projected history exceeds
token or event ceiling?

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No windowing
preserve full projected history

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Protect summaries / working set
inject durable working set after compaction or restore

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Group causal chunks
tool Action + matching Observation stay together

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Select newest whole chunks backward
enforce minimum recent tool loops
and minimum tail token floor

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
If the newest required chunk alone is too large,
truncate that copy to the remaining budget
never mutate the ledger event

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Bounded prompt-history projection
protected facts + intact recent causality

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY WINDOW BEFORE SUMMARIZING?
Problem: every transformation can lose information, and many over-budget moments can be solved by omitting old operational noise rather than inventing a new narrative.
Chosen: first build a reversible model-facing selection over the immutable ledger; compact only when sustained boundary pressure requires a new summary.
Why not summarize on every turn: added model latency/cost, semantic drift, and summaries of summaries. Why not raw tail truncation: it may remove the Action while retaining its Observation or erase durable anchors.
Consequence: cheap predictable pressure control with full audit history intact; older unselected detail is unavailable to that inference turn unless recalled.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY CAUSAL CHUNKS, MINIMUM TOOL LOOPS, AND A TAIL FLOOR?
Action/result pairing: model APIs require coherent tool-call sequences and the result is meaningless without its request. Minimum loops: preserves enough recent think→act→observe examples for the model to know the current trajectory. Tail token floor: prevents many tiny protected events from crowding out the actual latest work.
Why not keep the last N events: N ignores token variance and can split pairs. Why not importance scoring here: selection must be deterministic, fast, and safe during emergency overflow.
Consequence: syntactically valid and operationally coherent prompts; some older high-value facts must survive through canonical state, summaries, or recall instead.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY MODEL-AWARE TOKEN BUDGETS WITH FIXED-PROMPT RESERVES?
Problem: the provider limit covers system text, tool schemas, dynamic context, history, and output—not history alone. Characters/token vary by model and by code/JSON density.
Chosen: derive usable input from model capability, reserve output, subtract measured fixed sections, apply catalog correction, and cache immutable event counts.
Why not len(text)/4 only: acceptable fallback, unsafe as the primary gate. Why not wait for provider rejection: overflow recovery occurs after latency and may lose the turn.
Consequence: proactive, model-portable limits; catalogs and estimates can still be conservative or stale.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY TRUNCATE A DEEP-COPIED VIEW AT SAFE BOUNDARIES?
Problem: trimming the durable Event object would make replay/audit depend on whichever model happened to need a smaller prompt. Cutting raw structured text can leave broken JSON/XML/tool envelopes that invite hallucinated continuation.
Chosen: copy model-facing events, prefer newline then whitespace cuts, add visible markers, and preserve opening/closing section tags.
Why not invisible hard byte cuts: they conceal missing evidence and corrupt structure.
Consequence: the model knows information is incomplete while the evidence plane remains lossless.

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Extract current task terms
split camelCase · snake_case · paths
remove generic coding stop words

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Enumerate source candidates
git ls-files + untracked, else bounded walk
ignore build/cache/vendor paths

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deterministic first-turn signals
explicit path mention · dirty file
path/stem overlap · bounded rg content hits
matching Python symbols

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Lazy workspace symbol index
SQLite cache · hash + mtime freshness
Tree-sitter; Python AST fallback

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
File import graph
src file → imported workspace file

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Personalization prior per indexed file
0.2 base + task score + entrypoint boost

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Personalized PageRank
damping 0.85 · fixed 24 iterations
normalize every iteration

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Final rank
graph centrality + task score + entrypoint boost
deterministic path tie-break

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Token-bounded <REPO_MAP>
ranked paths + up to 4 public signatures/file
binary search maximum prefix fitting map_tokens

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
First-turn <CODING_PREFLIGHT>
top 6 candidates + reasons + dirty files
hints only; verify before editing

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Successful file mutation invalidates that path
repo map cache marked dirty and lazily rebuilt

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY RANK THE REPOSITORY AT ALL?
Problem: the whole repo rarely fits, but forcing the model to begin with blind glob/read loops wastes turns and may anchor on the wrong subsystem.
Chosen: provide a cheap structural prior: likely files and public symbols, never full contents.
Why not inject the complete tree/content: token cost grows with repo size and low-signal names crowd out task evidence. Why not provide nothing: every turn pays discovery latency and small models struggle to form a global map.
Consequence: faster orientation and architectural awareness; ranking can be wrong, so candidates are explicitly non-authoritative and source reads remain mandatory.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY THESE FIRST-PASS SIGNALS?
Explicit path mention is highest-precision user intent. Dirty files represent the workspace’s active delta. Path/stem overlap captures naming conventions cheaply. Bounded content hits find concepts not encoded in filenames. Matching symbols provide a semantic breadcrumb without loading bodies.
Why deterministic before embeddings: zero model call, explainable scores, immediate startup, cross-language fallback, and stable tests.
Consequence: excellent lexical precision and predictable cost; synonyms and conceptual relationships can be missed.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY PERSONALIZED PAGERANK ON IMPORTS?
Problem: lexical relevance finds files named like the task but misses architectural hubs, adapters, and dependencies that connect the change.
Chosen: import edges approximate dependency influence; PageRank propagates importance transitively, while task personalization teleports probability toward the current request.
Why damping 0.85: most weight follows architecture, while 15% restart prevents sinks/cycles from owning the ranking. Why 24 iterations: fixed bounded work gives stable practical convergence without a data-dependent latency tail.
Why not degree count: it sees only immediate neighbors. Why not pure semantic vectors: heavier, opaque, optional dependencies, and weaker explicit topology.
Consequence: task-focused structural centrality; dynamic imports and non-code relationships remain imperfect.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY BOOST ENTRYPOINTS AND ADD TASK SCORE TWICE?
Entrypoint boost: manifests, CLI/bootstrap files, and common roots explain how the system starts even when few files import them.
Task score in personalization: influences graph flow toward the task neighborhood. Task score in the final sum: preserves a direct relevance vote so a central but unrelated hub cannot dominate.
Alternative rejected: one opaque learned score that is difficult to debug or tune.
Consequence: an intentionally biased engineering heuristic—not a claim of mathematically pure ranking.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY PATHS + FOUR PUBLIC SIGNATURES UNDER A HARD TOKEN BUDGET?
Paths reveal module boundaries; signatures reveal available concepts and call surfaces; bodies would consume the budget before the model chooses what to inspect.
Four symbols caps per-file dominance. Public-first favors architectural API over implementation noise. Binary search finds the longest ranked prefix that fits without repeatedly trimming arbitrary text.
Why not character truncation: tokenizer density varies and a hard cut can split a structural entry.
Consequence: compact, syntactically intact orientation; private internals appear only after targeted reads.

div.style: color: rgb(20, 83, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Controller subscriber
reduce events into AgentState + session state

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
step() request funnel
call_soon_threadsafe to main loop
integer counter preserves every wakeup

div.style: color: rgb(20, 83, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One active inference step
asyncio.Lock + bounded request drain

div.style: color: rgb(20, 83, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Focused orchestration services
lifecycle · pending · retry · recovery
stuck · safety · validation · routing

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Pending-action table
Action.id ↔ Observation.cause

div.style: color: rgb(19, 78, 74) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ContextPipeline.prepare_step
project current ledger view

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY PROJECT STATE FROM EVENTS?
Problem: the UI, controller, recovery logic, and audit need different views of the same run.
Chosen: keep immutable facts central and build purpose-specific current-state projections.
Why not one giant mutable State object shared everywhere: consumers would silently overwrite each other and restart could not prove how values were derived.
Consequence: replayable, testable reducers and independent read models; projection lag and reducer versioning must be managed.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY ONE STEP OWNER?
Problem: model calls are state transitions, not independent HTTP requests. Concurrent steps could read the same history, spend twice, and emit conflicting actions.
Chosen: all step requests enter the main asyncio loop; a counter prevents lost wakeups and a lock admits one inference step at a time.
Why not recursive callbacks or one task per event: they create cross-loop races and duplicate reasoning turns that look like model hallucination.
Consequence: causal clarity and deterministic spend; theoretical turn throughput is intentionally sacrificed.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY EXPLICIT ACTION→OBSERVATION CAUSE IDS?
Problem: parallel or delayed tools make temporal adjacency unreliable: the next observation is not necessarily the result of the previous action.
Chosen: Observation.cause carries the durable Action ID; pending state clears by identity, not position.
Why not infer pairing from timestamps/order: worker scheduling, retries, and streaming output break that assumption.
Consequence: exact latency, retry, barrier, and audit attribution; every runtime path must preserve correlation.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A THIN ORCHESTRATOR OVER FOCUSED SERVICES?
Problem: lifecycle, retry, safety, pending work, and recovery interact but change for different reasons.
Chosen: SessionOrchestrator coordinates named services through a narrow OrchestrationContext facade.
Why not a multi-thousand-line controller: hidden cross-feature mutation makes local reasoning and testing impossible. Why not independent microservices: process/network boundaries add no value inside one local session.
Consequence: visible responsibilities and isolated tests; more modules and a facade that must resist becoming a service locator.

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
EventStream.publish
monotonic session ID · timestamp · source
secret masking

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Serialize typed payload
embedded ID + checksum

div.style: color: rgb(30, 41, 59) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Authoritative SQLite append
BEGIN IMMEDIATE · INSERT only
WAL journal · synchronous FULL

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Arm pending Action after durable identity
before inline delivery can produce an Observation

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Delivery policy

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Inline USER / CLI path
same-stack causal ordering

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Bounded worker queue
backpressure metrics

div.style: color: rgb(30, 58, 138) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One fact, multiple projections
controller · runtime · memory · UI

div.style: color: rgb(127, 29, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
If SQLite append fails, do not fall back to event JSON.
Two writable stores would create split-brain history.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY APPEND-ONLY EVENTS?
Problem: a mutable status row shows where the agent is, not which decision caused which side effect or what was known before failure.
Chosen: facts receive new IDs and are inserted once; corrections are later facts, never rewrites.
Why not CRUD mutation: updates erase intermediate states, complicate concurrent readers, and make crash timing indistinguishable from legitimate absence.
Consequence: temporal auditability, causal debugging, replay, and sequential writes; costs are log growth, projection code, schema evolution, and snapshots/indexes.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY EVENT SOURCING, NOT MERELY LOGGING?
Logging describes work after hidden application state changed. Event sourcing here makes Action and Observation the contract from which controller state, UI, memory, audit, and recovery views are projected.
Why not controller→runtime calls plus logs: direct calls create a second invisible truth and couple each consumer to the caller.
Consequence: one causal vocabulary across control, execution, persistence, and presentation; ordering and projection consistency become explicit architectural duties.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY SQLITE AS THE AUTHORITATIVE LOCAL LEDGER?
Workload: one local writer, many readers, append-heavy records, long ordered scans, and crash recovery.
Chosen: per-session embedded transactions and indexes with no service process.
Why not one JSON file per event: directory/fsync overhead and expensive long scans. Why not Postgres/Redis: operational infrastructure exceeds a single-user tool’s needs.
Consequence: atomic local truth and simple deployment; locking/corruption risk is concentrated, so serialized writes, checksums, integrity checks, and explicit degraded health are required.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY WRITE-AHEAD LOGGING, AND WHICH WAL?
Crash window: the process may die after intent is accepted but before final data pages are durable.
SQLite WAL: changed pages enter a sequential journal before database checkpoint; readers keep a stable snapshot while the writer advances. FULL synchronous favors crash truth over maximum throughput.
Legacy application WAL: only with SQLite disabled, write .pending JSON before the canonical event file, then remove it; restart cleans or replays the marker.
Why not silent fallback: recovery cannot reason safely about two authorities.
Consequence: deterministic crash recovery at the cost of extra writes and checkpoint cleanup.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY PERSIST BEFORE DELIVERY?
Problem: if a subscriber executes a tool and the process dies before its Action is durable, the workspace has an orphaned side effect.
Chosen: assign ID, sanitize, and persist first; then arm cause correlation and notify subscribers.
Why not fire-and-forget persistence: a small latency win is not worth unexplainable machine state.
Consequence: every dispatched action has durable lineage; storage latency enters turn latency.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY INLINE DELIVERY FOR THE CONTROL-CRITICAL PATH?
Problem: an extremely fast runtime can emit an Observation before an asynchronously delivered Action has registered its pending cause.
Chosen: USER and single-session CLI delivery stays inline; higher-volume paths may use bounded workers.
Why not thread-pool everything: throughput would introduce a causality race exactly where ordering matters most.
Consequence: deterministic pending/cause correlation; slow inline subscribers can delay publication.

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer input
Textual composer · piped stdin · CLI arguments

div.style: color: rgb(20, 83, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
launch.entry → backend.cli.entry

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY EXPLICIT CHAT / PLAN / AGENT MODES?
Problem: answering, planning, and mutating a machine have different social and safety contracts.
Chosen: one identity, memory, and ledger; tool availability and finish behavior vary by mode.
Why not specialist agents: handoffs duplicate context, lose rationale, and blur task ownership. Why not one unrestricted mode: read-only intent could cause side effects.
Consequence: continuity without role-transfer loss, with small mode-specific prompt/tool branches.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY A WORKSPACE-SCOPED DATA ROOT?
Problem: sessions, task state, indexes, and checkpoints must not collide across repositories or pollute source control.
Chosen: derive a stable workspace identity and store operational artifacts under the user data directory.
Why not .grinta in every repo: it dirties worktrees, risks accidental commits, and makes project permissions govern agent state.
Consequence: clean repositories and continuity per workspace; identity migration and path resolution require care.

div.style: color: rgb(113, 63, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WHY TWO PRESENTATION PATHS?
Problem: humans need incremental cards and confirmation dialogs; pipes and CI need stable text and process completion.
Chosen: both subscribe to the same semantic event stream but own separate rendering/lifecycle adapters.
Why not make Textual pretend to be non-interactive: terminal capabilities and blocking behavior differ fundamentally.
Consequence: honest automation and rich interaction; some presentation logic is duplicated.

span.p:
GRINTA — LINEAR ARCHITECTURE ARGUMENT
Developer intent → grounded context → model decision → governed side effect → durable evidence → final answer
Each major mechanism explains its problem, chosen strategy, rejected alternatives, and consequence.
